summary: Go SDK: idempotency key prefixing by orchestrator leads to duplicate function/tool invocations
description: Customer reports repeated duplicate downstream tool/webhook invocations originating from a long-running, multiplexed orchestration flow that uses per-action idempotency semantics. The Go SDK + their orchestrator appear to be prefixing the idempotency key with a shard/orch token before each sub-request; in some cases the prefixed key is truncated by an edge proxy, resulting in collisions and duplicate side effects.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sets up a multiplexed orchestration: one client request expands into 3 tool/function calls (payment-check, inventory-reserve, send-webhook).
2) Go SDK version used: v1.4.2; orchestration middleware attaches idempotency: 'origKey-<timestamp>'. Orchestrator inserts per-shard prefix 'shard-<n>:' to create sub-keys.
3) Client executes request; network path includes their edge sidecar -> cloud edge proxy -> redwood api-gateway -> serving runtime.
4) Under intermittent retry/backoff (simulated by killing sidecar for 1s), downstream webhook sometimes receives duplicated POSTs for the same payment/inventory action.

5) Observed behaviour: two separate funcall confirmations recorded by the customer's backend, both with different idempotency headers (after prefixing) but identical truncated prefix leading to collisions.
logs: 2026-03-09T15:12:03Z [orchestrator] expanding request id=abc123 -> subcalls [shard-0:origKey-161790, shard-1:origKey-161790, shard-2:origKey-161790]
2026-03-09T15:12:05Z [serving-runtime] delivered funcall payment-check accept=true idempotency=shard-1:origKey-161 (collision observed)
Customer webhook received 2 POSTs within 2s with identical truncated payload correlation id=abc123
customer_observed_impact: Duplicate charges/reservations visible in customer's test environment for ~0.2% of orchestrated requests. They have disabled the flow in production until we provide mitigation guidance.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: duplicates occur only on multiplexed flows where orchestrator prepends a shard prefix to the idempotency key.
Edge proxy (third-party sidecar) is configured with a 64-byte header size limit and rewrites headers; confirmed by customer's networking team.
When prefix+origKey length exceeds the proxy limit, proxy truncates the header mid-token causing different prefixed keys to hash/collapse to the same value downstream.
Go SDK does not currently canonicalize or hash idempotency keys before sending; orchestrator relies on raw prefixing semantics.
Reproduced in-house by running their sidecar with limit=20 bytes: observed same truncation and duplicate downstream calls.
Hypothesis: header-truncation collision is main cause. Secondary factors: different encodings of separator (colon vs dot) may change truncation boundary but not eliminate collision risk.
workarounds_provided: 1) Short-term: Ask customer to enable per-action deterministic hashing on their orchestrator so prefixed keys are SHA256(origKey + shard) hex-encoded and then truncated to 32 chars (avoid raw prefixing that exceeds proxy limits).
2) Ask customer to increase allowed header size on the edge sidecar (recommended) so full prefixed keys are preserved.
3) If increasing header size is not possible, suggest moving idempotency token into the POST body as 'idempotency_key' and use the SDK/endpoint that reads from body (this bypasses header limits).

4) Temporary SDK option: set environment variable REDWOOD_DISABLE_IDEMPOTENCY_PREFIX to true to stop orchestrator/plugin from auto-prefixing keys (requires orchestrator change), or use per-action explicit keys.
Customer applied workaround #1 in staging and reported no duplicate webhooks for 24h test window; they are testing in canary now.
resolution: Mitigation accepted by customer: orchestration team implemented deterministic per-action hashing and updated their canary to use hashed idempotency keys; duplicates stopped in canary. SRE to follow up with long-term fixes: document header-size guidance, add SDK helper to produce stable hashed idempotency keys, and add API-side normalization to deduplicate truncated collisions when possible.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: Add a helper function to Go SDK that returns a stable hashed idempotency key given a base key and action shard (owner: go-sdk team, ETA 2026-03-20).
2) Docs: Publish a short KB on header limits and recommended idempotency key strategies (owner: docs/devexp, ETA 2026-03-18).
3) Product/SRE: Evaluate API-gateway tolerant normalization to avoid obvious truncation collisions server-side (investigate tradeoffs for opacity vs correctness).
4) Follow up with customer on 2026-03-16 to confirm production rollout and close ticket if no regression for 72 hours.
